backlog.title: Thermal Co-Simulation Testing Of Co-Packaged Optics
backlog.summary:
Ensuring optical engines can operate reliably alongside high-power AI processors in multi-chip packages.
The post Thermal Co-Simulation Testing Of Co-Packaged Optics appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Co-packaged optics (CPO) are essential for scaling data center interconnects, but they introduce significant thermal management challenges in high-power AI packages.
Thermal co-simulation results demonstrate that CPO can operate reliably within a 3 kW power envelope when integrated into advanced multi-chip packages.
The design utilizes a 9-2-9 layer substrate and UCIe interfaces to support over 100 Tbps of optical bandwidth, proving that optical engines can coexist with high-performance AI silicon.

backlog.title: Why Open-Weight AI Matters
backlog.summary:
Proprietary models still hold the edge, but open-weight models add more flexibility for deploying AI.
The post Why Open-Weight AI Matters appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Open-weight AI models allow users to host and adapt models locally, reducing vendor lock-in and enabling deployment on custom hardware.
Hardware architects must now design for adaptability, as model architectures evolve in weeks while silicon development cycles take years.
The shift toward trillion-parameter models and open-weight availability is driving a need for hardware that can handle sparse computation and rapidly changing numeric formats.

backlog.title: Building AI Infrastructure For Greater Choice And Flexibility
backlog.summary:
Open interfaces and interoperability allow designers to choose technologies based on the needs of the system.
The post Building AI Infrastructure For Greater Choice And Flexibility appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: AI infrastructure is shifting toward heterogeneous architectures because training and inference workloads have distinct requirements for memory, latency, and throughput.
Open standards like UCIe are critical for enabling a chiplet-based ecosystem, allowing architects to mix and match compute, I/O, and memory interfaces from different vendors.
Standardized die-to-die connectivity provides the flexibility to partition functions within a package, helping designers balance performance, power, and cost more effectively.

backlog.title: Strengthening Advanced-Node Interconnects Through Automated Via Insertion
backlog.summary:
Short-resilient via insertion improves reliability and performance.
The post Strengthening Advanced-Node Interconnects Through Automated Via Insertion appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: At sub-5nm nodes, via resistance increases exponentially, making vertical interconnects a primary bottleneck for power, performance, and area (PPA).
High via resistance exacerbates electromigration and IR drop, which can lead to timing failures or permanent silicon damage if not addressed during the design phase.
Manual via insertion is no longer feasible due to layout density, necessitating automated, signoff-aware optimization to maintain reliability and time-to-market.

backlog.title: Pig kidneys that were “frozen” for a year have been brought back to life
backlog.summary: Pig kidneys that were cooled to -150 °C and stored in a freezer for months have been successfully rewarmed and shown to work again for the first time, say scientists. They hope to replicate the findings with human organs. The kidneys—which are similar in size to human ones—were left in a glass-like state, in one…
bullets: Researchers have achieved a breakthrough in cryopreservation by successfully storing and rewarming pig kidneys, a process that could eventually allow for the indefinite banking of human organs.
Current organ transplantation is severely limited by a 24-to-36-hour viability window, which creates significant logistical challenges and contributes to the global organ shortage.
While the current results are a milestone, the researchers have yet to prove that these organs can sustain long-term life, and the findings have not yet undergone peer review.
The ability to bank organs would fundamentally transform the transplant market, potentially reducing the reliance on immunosuppressive drugs and improving matching efficiency for patients.

backlog.title: Why Physical AI Is So Hard To Engineer
backlog.summary:
Integrating sensors, compute, and actuators into autonomous systems adds new challenges for chip design.
The post Why Physical AI Is So Hard To Engineer appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Physical AI represents a shift from generative text/code models to systems that must perceive, decide, and act autonomously within unstructured physical environments.
The transition to physical AI introduces critical safety requirements, where a 1% error rate can have life-or-death consequences, necessitating new design methodologies and simulation tools.

Industry experts emphasize that physical AI is as much an imaging and sensor-fusion challenge as it is a compute challenge, requiring tighter integration between sensing, inference, and real-time control.

backlog.title: How far can we push computing?
backlog.summary: MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of science and technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can read more from the series here. On the evening of December 29, 1959, at an American Physical Society meeting at Caltech, the physicist Richard Feynman gave a lecture called “There’s…
bullets: The tech industry is currently relying on 'brute force' scaling, with hyperscalers projected to spend over $700 billion on infrastructure in 2026, doubling the record set in 2025.
Traditional performance gains driven by Moore’s Law and Dennard’s Law are stalling, forcing a transition from easy miniaturization to the physical limits of atomic-scale computing.

The massive capital expenditure on data centers is outpacing the capacity of the electrical grid, highlighting a growing tension between the demand for AI compute and the physical constraints of energy and hardware density.

backlog.title: Do You Trust Apple?
backlog.summary: Apple has a lot of trust in terms of delivering integrated products and preserving privacy; the real trust question is if you think Siri AI will justify investing more in their ecosystem.

The introduction of AirPort demonstrated Apple's ability to adopt open industry standards like 802.11 while simultaneously differentiating through superior industrial design and seamless hardware integration.

By embedding antennas directly into the iBook chassis and simplifying the user experience, Apple successfully commoditized the underlying wireless technology while maintaining a premium brand position.
The core value proposition of 'ease-of-use combined with privacy' remains the foundational pillar of Apple's business model, influencing how the company approaches new technological shifts today.

backlog.summary:

bullets: The new AMBA C2C specification aims to unify chip-to-chip connectivity by supporting both AXI and CHI protocols under a single, scalable framework.
By utilizing protocol subsetting, AMBA C2C allows implementations to scale complexity based on specific use cases, such as simple I/O attachment versus fully coherent superchips.
This converged approach addresses the need for greater reuse and interoperability across the vast installed base of AXI-based designs in the chiplet ecosystem.

backlog.title: Beyond The Specification: What Really Determines PCIe Retimer Reach?
backlog.summary:
Multiple interacting factors span silicon design, controller intelligence, channel quality, and the transmission medium itself.
The post Beyond The Specification: What Really Determines PCIe Retimer Reach? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: PCIe retimer reach is determined by a combination of SerDes architecture, controller intelligence, and channel quality rather than just specification compliance.
While standard specifications often target 36 dB of insertion loss at Nyquist, leading retimer vendors are engineering for 40 dB or higher to provide greater deployment flexibility.
The ability to exceed standard loss budgets allows designers to accommodate more connectors, longer PCB traces, and manufacturing variations without requiring costly board redesigns.

backlog.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”

The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to…
bullets: Researchers testing Claude Opus 4.7 in a simulated environment observed the agents engaging in 'playful' behaviors, including rule-making and goal-setting, without human intervention.

The study suggests a potential shift in AI training from traditional supervised or reinforcement learning toward 'playful learning,' where models develop capabilities through self-directed exploration.

The agents exhibited four hallmarks of play, including repeating activities with variations and pretending objects had different functions, which could inform future development of more autonomous and creative AI systems.

backlog.title: Inside the quest to combat Arctic fires and save the planet’s frozen carbon
backlog.summary: In the middle of an especially warm July in 2021, a wildfire ignited in a thick forest of black spruce and peeling paper birch trees on the northern campus of the University of Alaska, Fairbanks.  The blaze, possibly sparked by lightning, burned across the dry carpet of feather mosses and lichen before climbing into the…
bullets: Wildfires are stripping away the insulating moss and organic soil layers of the boreal forest, causing the underlying permafrost to thaw significantly faster than in undisturbed areas.
The thawing of permafrost poses a major climate risk, as it releases trapped greenhouse gases that further accelerate global warming, creating a dangerous feedback loop.
Scientists are currently evaluating the efficacy of fire-spotting satellites and AI-driven monitoring tools to better manage and prevent fires in northern latitudes to preserve carbon sinks.

bullets: MIT and EPFL engineers have developed a 300-gram 'flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle' (FAAV) capable of both flight and underwater swimming.
The robot utilizes flexible wings coated in hydrophobic nanoparticles and a motorized tail to transition seamlessly between air and water mediums.
By eliminating the need for feet during takeoff, the design offers a cost-effective, agile platform for environmental monitoring, such as sampling near icebergs or tracking marine life.

backlog.title: A reason to eat carbs
backlog.summary: A high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet can help some people lose weight, and some research has shown that it may protect against colon cancer. But a new study suggests that such a ketogenic diet may also increase the risk of cancer in the small intestine. This type of diet forces the body to burn fatty acids instead…
bullets: MIT research indicates that while ketogenic diets may suppress colon tumors, they can simultaneously increase the risk of tumor growth in the small intestine.
The study found that high-fat diets trigger fatty acid oxidation, which accelerates the multiplication of intestinal stem cells and inadvertently promotes tumor formation.
The findings suggest that the metabolic effects of diet are highly localized within the gut, cautioning against broad generalizations regarding the health benefits of ketogenic protocols.

bullets: An MIT historian debunked the historical authenticity of a tea chest label previously associated with the 1773 Boston Tea Party.
Linguistic analysis of Cantonese characters revealed the label actually originated from a 19th-century US trading firm, Smith, Archer & Co.
The study highlights how historical artifacts can acquire false narratives over time, emphasizing the importance of rigorous provenance research in museum collections.

backlog.title: Nuclear-powered spaceships
backlog.summary: Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era…
bullets: NASA is investing $2 billion into nuclear electric propulsion, which utilizes uranium-atom-splitting reactions to generate electricity for ion-based thrust.
The agency plans to launch the uncrewed Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) mission to Mars by late 2028, aiming to significantly reduce travel time and cosmic radiation exposure for future astronauts.

While previous programs like DRACO were canceled due to high costs and safety testing challenges, experts believe nuclear propulsion is technically viable and essential for efficient interplanetary travel.

backlog.title: Exercise in a pill
backlog.summary: We all know exercise is good for us. It builds muscle, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and boosts mood. By deciphering how movement benefits the body, researchers hope to develop medicines that can offer some of the same perks—without the workout. The idea isn’t to replace exercise but to bring its upsides to people who…
bullets: Researchers are identifying molecular pathways triggered by physical activity to develop pharmaceuticals that mimic the health benefits of exercise for patients with frailty or chronic illness.
The biotech firm Pelagos is developing a compound that targets specific receptors in muscle cells to boost endurance, with early mouse studies showing improved cognitive and heart health.
Regulatory hurdles remain significant, as the FDA currently approves drugs for disease treatment rather than wellness enhancement, and over 90% of human clinical trials fail.

backlog.title: Cleaning up PFAS
backlog.summary: Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a.k.a. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond…
bullets: PFAS 'forever chemicals' are pervasive in the environment, with 89% of the US population showing blood plasma levels above common thresholds for potential health risks.
Current cleanup efforts focus on trapping chemicals via reverse osmosis or foam fractionation, though these methods leave behind contaminated brine that requires expensive destruction.
Electrochemical degradation, a method using electrodes to break down the carbon-fluorine bonds in PFAS, has demonstrated over 90% efficiency in tests and is being commercialized by AECOM.

The industry is facing significant challenges in managing data streams in heterogeneous architectures, necessitating new approaches to chip design and interconnect scaling.

Testing high-power ASICs alongside optical engines presents significant challenges in power delivery and thermal management, complicating the transition to parallel testing.

bullets: New Fab Technology Co-Optimization (FTCO) workflows now integrate GDS layout data with 3D process simulation and AI-based surrogate modeling to account for real-world fabrication variations.
GPU-accelerated FDTD simulations can now process complex 3D models with 65 million cells in under 10 hours, significantly speeding up design cycles.
The use of digital twins allows non-simulation experts to intuitively understand the relationship between manufacturing process variations and final photonic circuit performance.

backlog.summary: Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us. backlog.title: Eliminating traffic deaths
backlog.summary: Every year, traffic crashes kill more than one million people, and they’re the leading cause of death for children and young adults. bullets: Traffic crashes kill over one million people annually, making them a leading cause of preventable death for children and young adults globally.

Cities like Hoboken, New Jersey, have achieved zero traffic fatalities since 2017 by implementing infrastructure changes such as curb extensions, improved public transit, and data-driven intersection redesigns.
Widespread adoption of safety measures is often hindered by government bureaucracy and the difficulty of justifying the removal of parking or road space for pedestrian-focused infrastructure.
